title: Cold sores: early care, reducing transmission and warning signs
intro: Cold sores are outbreaks of herpes simplex infection, usually causing painful blisters on or near the lips. Tingling, itching or burning may start before the blisters appear. The virus can remain inactive and later reactivate, so a recurrence does not necessarily mean a new infection. Many episodes settle on their own, while early treatment can shorten symptoms. Protection of newborns and prompt assessment of eye symptoms are particularly important.

sections.heading: Check that the pattern is familiar
paragraphs: A typical episode progresses from tingling to grouped blisters, then crusting and healing. The first symptomatic infection can be more widespread, with painful gums, sores inside the mouth and fever. Not every cracked lip, mouth ulcer or crusted patch is herpes; impetigo and other conditions may need different treatment. Ask for assessment if the appearance is unusual, very extensive or not beginning to heal after about ten days. Difficulty drinking because of painful mouth sores needs earlier advice.

sections.heading: Reduce contact while a sore is developing and healing
paragraphs: Avoid kissing and oral sex from the first warning tingling until the area has completely healed. Oral herpes can cause genital infection through oral contact. Avoid touching the sore and wash hands before and after applying treatment; take care not to touch the eyes. Do not share lip products or items in contact with saliva. Transmission can sometimes occur without visible sores, so these precautions reduce risk rather than guaranteeing none. Discuss concerns with partners without blaming someone for when infection was acquired.

sections.heading: Ease discomfort and use medicines appropriately
paragraphs: Keep drinking and avoid foods that sting. A pharmacist can advise a suitable pain-relieving product, protective patch or antiviral cream. Antiviral treatment for recurrent sores works best started at the earliest signs and provides limited benefit rather than removing the virus from the body. Follow age restrictions and instructions, and keep ordinary lip preparations out of the eye. A clinician may prescribe tablets for particularly severe, frequent or troublesome episodes. Do not use someone else's prescription or assume that a patch makes kissing safe.

sections.heading: A recurrence plan can make episodes easier to manage
paragraphs: Illness, sunlight, stress or hormonal changes can trigger reactivation in some people. Notice your own pattern without assuming every episode has an avoidable cause. Suitable sun protection for the lips can help when sunlight is a trigger. Ask whether keeping treatment available or a preventive prescription is appropriate if episodes are frequent or disruptive. Recurrences can be frustrating and affect confidence, but herpes is common and does not indicate poor hygiene or personal failure. Review a changing pattern rather than continually treating an uncertain diagnosis.

sections.heading: Protect babies and recognise urgent problems
paragraphs: Do not kiss a baby when you have a cold sore, and follow careful hand hygiene before necessary care. Herpes in a newborn can be serious. Seek urgent medical advice if a young baby is feeding poorly, has fever or develops sores; unusual sleepiness, floppiness, breathing difficulty or a seizure needs emergency help, even without blisters. Eye pain, redness with worsening vision or light sensitivity needs urgent eye care. People with weakened immunity or widespread painful blistering should seek prompt assessment. Do not treat a suspected eye infection with ordinary cold-sore cream.

examples.title: Visiting a new baby — hypothetical example
examples.text: A visitor notices tingling at the lip before a planned visit. They avoid kissing the baby and discuss safer contact with the family. They do not assume the absence of a visible blister removes the risk.

examples.title: A new eye symptom — hypothetical example
examples.text: A person with a familiar lip sore develops a painful red eye and blurred vision. They seek urgent eye assessment rather than putting lip cream near the eye or waiting for the lip lesion to heal.
